answer.evidence: radon/raw.py:82-93 `_split_tokens(tokens, token, value)` starts with `res = [[]]` and iterates the tokens. When `(token, value) == token_values[:2]` it appends a new empty list and `continue`s, so the separator is never added to any partition. Every other token is appended to `res[-1]`. Empty partitions are kept: consecutive separators, a leading separator and a trailing separator each produce an empty list. An empty input returns `[[]]`. Review items: add tests for those edge cases, and check the callers of `_split_tokens` in raw.py to see whether they expect empty partitions. A grep for split/partition/separator in radon/ found no equivalent logic in complexity.py, metrics.py or visitors.py. They get only brief confirmation time.

            return len(tokens) - index - 1
    raise ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')


def _split_tokens(tokens, token, value):
    '''Split a list of tokens on the specified token pair (token, value),
    where *token* is the token type (i.e. its code) and *value* its actual
    value in the code.
    '''
    res = [[]]
    for token_values in tokens:
        if (token, value) == token_values[:2]:
            res.append([])
            continue
        res[-1].append(token_values)
    return res


def _get_all_tokens(line, lines):
    '''Starting from *line*, generate the necessary tokens which represent the
    shortest tokenization possible. This is done by catching
    :exc:`tokenize.TokenError` when a multi-line string or statement is
    encountered.
    :returns: tokens, lines
    '''
    buffer = line
    used_lines = [line]
